# How AI Image Style References Work: A Plain-English Guide

You've probably seen those striking AI-generated images online — a moody film still, a hand-drawn sketch, a neon-soaked 1980s poster. Wondering how people get such different looks from the same tool? There's a feature for that, and it's called **style references**.

## What a style reference actually is

A style reference is a way to tell an AI image generator: "Make this image, but make it look like that." You give it a subject (like "a beachside café at sunset") and a style cue (the look — watercolour, vintage film, comic book, and so on).

In **Midjourney**, one of the most popular AI image tools, this is handled through a **parameter** (a little tag you add to your prompt) called **--sref** (short for "style reference"). You can either pass it a link to an image whose style you want to copy, or type **--sref random** to let Midjourney pick a style for you.

This is different from "style prompting," where you describe the look in words. Style references let the AI look at an actual image and borrow its visual feel — colour palette, brushwork, mood, lighting.

## Why this matters now

A few days ago, AI image tools were back in the news, and features like style references are a big reason why. For everyday creators, this is a quiet shift. Instead of hoping the AI picks a good look, you can guide it.

What it changes:

- It saves time. No more regenerating the same image twenty times trying to get the right mood
- It levels the playing field. You don't need to know art terms like "chiaroscuro" or "risograph" — you can just point at an image you like
- It opens up new workflows. You can build a small "style library" of references for different projects

## Try it yourself

The easiest way to explore this is with a Midjourney account. You'll need a **Discord** account to sign up — that's the chat platform Midjourney runs through.

Once you're in, open Midjourney (either inside Discord or at midjourney.com) and type a prompt like:

`/imagine prompt: a small bookshop on a rainy evening, warm window light --sref random`

Hit enter. Within a minute, you'll get four image variations, each in a different visual style. The bookshop stays the same; only the look changes. Some might feel like film stills, others like watercolours, others like graphic illustrations.

If you're using a different tool — DALL·E, Adobe Firefly, Stable Diffusion, or anything else — the exact command will differ, but the idea is the same. Most modern image generators now have some way to apply a style cue.

## A few tips for better results

- **Start with a clear subject.** Style references work best when your main image idea is well-defined. "A coffee cup on a wooden table" beats "something coffee-related"
- **Run the same prompt a few times.** You'll see different random styles each go
- **Save the styles you like.** Even ones you can't use right now. Build a small lookbook for future projects
- **Mix style cues with mood words.** Try `/imagine prompt: autumn forest path, golden hour --sref random` — combining a style cue with a mood description often gives richer results

## What this means for you

- **If you're a casual creator** (blogger, hobbyist, small business owner): style references let you produce on-brand visuals without hiring a designer for every project
- **If you work in marketing or design**: this is a fast way to mock up different visual directions for a campaign — show your team three or four moods in an hour, not a week
- **If you're just curious about AI image tools**: this is one of the friendliest features to experiment with. You don't need art vocabulary. The AI shows you the options

## Wrap-up

Style references turn AI image generation from "guess what the AI will do" into a real collaboration. You bring the idea, the AI shows you a spread of visual directions, and you pick the one that fits.

**Try this today**: sign into Midjourney (or whichever AI image tool you already use) and type `/imagine prompt: a friendly dog in a garden --sref random`. See what comes back. Pick the style that makes you smile.
